ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) are mentioned but not modeled in detail. Are these three separate value types on Vendor, or should they be structured further (street, city, etc.)? The transcript flags they are 'frequently different and frequently wrong' but no further structure or identification scheme is discussed.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Tax ID is explicitly stated as not unique across vendors (duplicates exist), yet it remains a candidate attribute on Vendor. Is Tax ID still worth modeling as a value type without any uniqueness constraint, or should it be modeled with a note that it may be shared by multiple legal entities/duplicate records?

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead? Dana: You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is used ambiguously by different stakeholders to mean two different concepts (spend tier vs risk tier), causing real confusion in meetings. Although the model separates them into SpendTier and RiskTier, the underlying naming/communication problem is unresolved organizationally.

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: And you both call it "tier." Raj: We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos.

ambiguities.description: Vendor duplication (same tax ID, same company onboarded twice) is a known unresolved data quality issue affecting compliance's ability to see aggregate exposure. Should the model include any distinction between a 'legal entity' concept and a 'vendor record' to eventually address this, or is it explicitly out of scope?

source_references.excerpt: Dana: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag exists informally in Mei's personal spreadsheet with no defined criteria or process. The facilitator explicitly decided not to model this since it's ad hoc. Should this be revisited if/when a formal rule is defined?

source_references.excerpt: Mei: There's a column called "preferred."... Facilitator: I'm going to note that as a gap rather than a rule... Mei: It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: What happens to in-flight Purchase Orders when a Vendor is suspended (e.g., a proposed 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and deferred to a steering group / Legal. No constraint should be modeled for this yet, but it represents an open business rule gap.

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The historical vendor statuses (pending, under review, inactive) were collapsed into three (draft, active, suspended) during a migration. Is any historical tracking of prior statuses needed, or is only current status relevant going forward?

source_references.excerpt: Dana: There used to be more. There was a "pending" and an "under review" and I think an "inactive," and they all got collapsed when we migrated.

ambiguities.description: RiskReview has a review ID for audit purposes ('who signed it and when') but the exact identifying scheme (is review_id alone sufficient, or is it combination with vendor?) is not fully detailed -- only that review_id exists and one review belongs to exactly one vendor. Also unclear whether signer and signed date are separate value types to be captured.

source_references.excerpt: Mei: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

ambiguities.description: Region count is described as 'four today' with talk of splitting EMEA -- is Region a fixed value type (four codes) or should it be treated as an open entity type since new regions may be added in the future?

source_references.excerpt: Mei: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM. ... Mei: Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.
Oh. Vendor number. Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.
Legal name. Tax ID. Address, though we have three addresses really
A vendor is identified by a vendor number. It has a legal name, a tax ID which is not unique
Dana: Draft, active, suspended. ... Mei: Collapsed into three, yes. Draft, active, suspended. That's what the field allows now. Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

Raj: Risk tier comes from the review, so a vendor without a review has no risk tier. Draft vendors don't have one.
